text: emmy: read P fully (distributed zeroth-order CVaR, bounds O(delta_max + e_s/delta_min), Thm 1 ergodic, Thm 2 last iterate, sampling condition (8) sum 1/(m sqrt s) <= e_s). Reading Q (LAA survey). First candidate line to test: P as a "prediction-free baseline" is the wrong reading; instead ask whether Q-style warm-start/learned predictions (predicted tail quantile tau, predicted optimizer, or predicted per-agent sample budget) can enter P with a consistency/robustness pair. Specific hook: RU representation min over tau; a predicted VaR tau_hat is a natural scalar prediction whose error |tau_hat - VaR| can control a CVaR estimator error. Will check whether that is real or cosmetic before posting a finding.

F1 (correction to P, derivation in emmy/F1_bias_artifact.md). P bounds the finite-sample gradient bias by D_x E||e_k^i|| <= D_x (d/delta) beta_i(s), giving the e_s/delta_min term in D_1, D_2 (Prop. iterate relation, Thm 1, Prop. liminf, Thm 2, centralized corollaries). But because the batch is fresh and independent of u (P Sec.3), E[hat g_k^i|F_k] is EXACTLY grad of the delta-smoothed expected empirical CVaR C^{i,s}_delta (P itself states this as eq. surrogate-unbiased-gradient in Thm 2), C^{i,s} is convex (P says so), and sup_x |C^{i,s}-C^i| <= beta_i(s)=sqrt(2pi)U_i/(alpha_i sqrt s) by P Lemma A.1 + DKW. A function-value step <grad tildeC(y),y-z> >= tildeC(y)-tildeC(z) >= C_delta(y)-C_delta(z)-2beta replaces the gradient-error step and yields D_2 = 2L delta_max + D_x L delta_max/r + 2 sqrt(2pi) max(U_i/alpha_i) e_s: no factor d, no 1/delta_min. In P own simulation (d=10, D_x~63, delta=0.4) the sampling term shrinks by d D_x/(2 delta) ~ 790x. Consequences: (i) P Remark 2 claim that diminishing delta_k forces growing s is wrong: fixed s, delta_k->0 gives limit O(e_s); (ii) the corrected order is attained by P algorithm: Bernoulli-at-alpha loss gives Theta(1/sqrt s) true excess, asymmetric V gives Theta(delta), so the plug-in fixed point is Theta(delta+e_s) (tight for this algorithm, not a minimax lower bound); (iii) P abstract claim that the distributed bound "matches the parameter dependence of the centralized benchmark" compares two achieved upper bounds sharing the same removable artifact; in Q Axis B terms (Q Sec 2.3, Axis B paragraph) this is E0 vs E0, a concrete case of why Q insists on same-model matching. Lifting tau (RU joint (x,tau_i), tau_i local, single sample) removes e_s entirely at a 1/alpha variance cost; checking literature now.

ada intention (round 1). Q=LAA survey (Zhao et al.), P=distributed zeroth-order CVaR (Wang, Huang, Xu, Johansson). Line I am pursuing: in P the one-point estimator g=(d/delta)*Chat(y+delta u)*u has two error channels, a BIAS channel (smoothing + finite-sample CVaR) and a VARIANCE channel (|g|<=dU/delta, the 1/delta_min^2 transient in Cor.1). (a) I am checking whether P overstates the bias: its surrogate identity E[g|F_k]=grad Ctilde(y) (proof of Thm 2) plus a UNIFORM value bound sup_x|Ctilde-C_delta|<=(U/alpha)sqrt(2pi/s) seems to give O(delta_max+e_s), not O(delta_max+e_s/delta_min). (b) If so, delta only hurts through variance, and that is where a prediction can enter with robustness by construction: subtract an F_k-measurable predicted CVaR value b (a baseline / control variate). E[u]=0 keeps the estimator unbiased for ANY b, so a bad prediction can only inflate variance (clip b to [-U,U] caps it at 4x P). This zero-mean-channel device (REINFORCE baselines, prediction-powered inference) is not one of Q P1-P5, and it discharges Q P4 obligations exactly, because |g|^2=(d/delta)^2 (Chat-b)^2 can be observed for every candidate baseline. Derivations will go in ada/. Emmy: please cross-check (a) independently. I am not looking at the composition propositions or the kappa-CR in depth, so those are open for you.

Cross-check of emmy #2 (F1): I derived the same correction independently before reading #2 (ada/derivations.md, section F1) and agree with every step. Refinement: the 2*beta can be beta. Empirical CVaR is biased DOWNWARD (Chat_s is a min over tau of a sample average, so E Chat_s <= C), hence Ctilde_s - C_delta lies in [-b_s, 0] uniformly and <grad Ctilde(y), y-z> >= C_delta(y) - C_delta(z) - b_s. 1-D illustration (ada/check_bias.py: J=|x-xi|, xi~Bern(0.3), alpha=0.5, X=[-1,2], exact Cbar_s): at s=4 the true gap of argmin_{X_delta} Ctilde falls from 0.043 (delta=0.4) to 0.0016 (delta=0.01), while P finite-sample term D_x d sqrt(2pi) U/(alpha delta) e_s grows from 38 to 1504. The Bernoulli-at-alpha bias matches sqrt((1-alpha)/(2 pi alpha s)) to 3 digits for s=16..1024, so Theta(1/sqrt s) holds. This illustrates the argument only; it cannot test an upper bound.

Cross-check of ada #3. (a) CONFIRMED independently (my #2, emmy/F1_bias_artifact.md) and numerically (emmy/check_tau_lift.py): on the Bernoulli instance (alpha=0.1, s=16, delta=0.3) P plug-in estimator converges in 200/200 runs to x=-0.697 = argmin of the surrogate over X_delta, true gap 0.1311 vs predicted 0.1313, i.e. the Theta(1/sqrt s) floor is real and exactly where F1 says. (b) Unbiasedness for any F_k-measurable b and the 4x cap after clipping: agree. Two qualifications. (1) Prior art: b = previous observed value is the one-point residual-feedback oracle (Zhang, Zhou, Ji, Zavlanos, Automatica 136:110006, 2022, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S000510982100532X ; arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.07378), and a distributed version exists (https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-981-95-3312-1_26). Inside Q, the closest relative is the OCO paragraph "Convex Optimization with Predictable Structure" (optimistic OMD hints, Rakhlin-Sridharan; Bhaskara et al.), which already has "bad hint costs at most a constant factor" robustness through sum ||g_t - hat g_t||^2. So "not one of P1-P5" is right as taxonomy, but a novelty claim should rest on the LAA contract (consistency/robustness pair, portfolio over baselines), not on the device. (2) In P the transient has two pieces: G^2 sum eta^2/sum eta (the 1/delta^2 piece, which your baseline improves via E||g||^2) and the disagreement piece L G sum eta^2/sum eta from Sundhar Ram Lemma 4.1, which is pathwise in G. It is linear in ||g_l||, so taking expectations lets E||g|| replace G; the check passes, but it has to be redone, not cited. (3) Your P4 full-information claim holds: (Chat - b_j)^2 is observable for every candidate b_j after one query.

F2 (pair-level; ada/derivations.md section F2). After F1, delta hurts P only through the VARIANCE channel, and that is where a Q-style prediction can enter with robustness by construction. Take g^b=(d/delta)(Chat_s(y+delta u)-b)u with b F_k-measurable (a predicted local CVaR value). (1) E[g^b|F_k]=grad Ctilde(y) for EVERY b because E u=0, so the corrected O(delta+e_s) bias bound holds for arbitrary predictions. (2) ||g^b||^2=(d/delta)^2 (Chat-b)^2 exactly. With eta=|C(y)-b|, E||g^b||^2 <= 3d^2(L^2+eta^2/delta^2+4U^2/(alpha^2 s delta^2)), vs P d^2U^2/delta^2. Consistency: free of delta except through s*delta^2. Smoothness: quadratic in eta/delta. Robustness: clip b to [-U,U] for a factor 4 on the worst-case bound. CAVEAT: that factor 4 is relative to P WORST-CASE bound, not to P realized (d/delta)^2 Chat^2, which is small when |C|<<U. In P sensor simulation C* is about 1e-3 while U is about 1e4, so b=0 is already near-oracle near x*, and a bad clipped b can be far worse than b=0 on that instance. (3) Fix: P4 aggregation over candidate baselines including b=0. Here it is EXACT, unlike Q generic P4 caveat, because the proof only needs the realized sum_k eta_k^2 (d/delta)^2 (Chat_k-b_k)^2 along the realized trajectory, and that loss can be observed for every candidate after each query: full information, no counterfactual state, no migration. Exp-concave aggregation then matches the best candidate (so at least b=0) up to an additive term. (4) The one-point estimator in P is NOT translation invariant: adding a constant c to every loss leaves the optimizer unchanged but inflates P variance by (d/delta)^2 c^2. A baseline restores invariance up to eta. P experiment has C* near 0, which favours b=0; checking this on P problem now. Prior art: residual feedback (b = own previous value) for ZO-CVaR already appears in P own reference wang2022risk (ICML 2022, arXiv 2203.08957), and P does not use it. The device is not new; what I claim, as a search result, is the LAA reading (bias-robustness for any prediction, exact P4 reduction) and that it sits outside Q P1-P5. Relative to emmy RU-lift: complementary. The lift removes the bias channel, the baseline shrinks the variance channel, and a lifted, baseline-subtracted estimator does both.

F2 (emmy/F2_tau_lift.md). Lifting the Rockafellar-Uryasev threshold into the decision moves ALL finite-sample CVaR error from the bias channel to the variance channel. phi_i(x,tau_i)=tau_i+(1/alpha_i)E(J^i(x,xi)-tau_i)_+ is jointly convex; tau_i stays local (no consensus on tau, only on x, so P communication pattern is unchanged); tau_i in [-U_i,U_i] loses nothing. A joint (d+1)-dim one-point estimator on (y, tau_i) using ONE sample per query is an unbiased gradient of the ball-smoothed phi_i, so the fixed point has bias O(L_phi delta) with no e_s term and no sampling condition (8); a batch of s only reduces variance. Price: L_phi <= sqrt(L^2+1)/alpha and |estimator| ~ (d+1)U(1+2/alpha)/delta, i.e. a 1/alpha factor in the worst-case smoothing bias and 1/alpha^2 in variance (second order in delta if the loss density at VaR is bounded). Numerics (emmy/check_tau_lift.py, same instance as above): tau-lift converges in 200/200 runs to x=+0.700 (true argmin end of X_delta), gap 0.0232 = pure X_delta shrinkage, vs plug-in gap 0.131. Caveat: that demo used x-ZO plus the exact tau-subgradient at the sphere point, a hybrid whose ball/sphere mismatch I have not analysed; the joint (d+1)-dim version is running now. SYNTHESIS with ada #3: after tau-lifting, sampling noise and baseline error both live only in the variance channel, where ada predicted baseline acts; the bias channel holds delta alone. Proposed joint line: "risk-averse ZO where every prediction and every sample affects only the transient", with an LAA contract: consistency = transient with a good baseline, robustness = 4x P transient, limiting neighborhood O(delta) regardless of prediction. Query run for prior work on tau-lifting in ZO CVaR: "zeroth-order CVaR optimization Rockafellar-Uryasev auxiliary variable joint one-point gradient estimator risk-averse"; it returned the KTH plug-in line (P; arXiv 2409.16866; 2512.22986; 2203.08957) and nothing joint. That is a record of the query, not a novelty claim. 2409.16866 also routes the empirical-CVaR error through (d/delta) eps_t u_t per its text, so F1 may apply to that line; its final bound is not yet checked.

Correction to my #7 (F2), from emmy/check_tau_joint.py; details appended to emmy/F2_tau_lift.md. The clean joint (d+1)-dim tau-lift, which smooths in tau too, pays its O(L delta/alpha) smoothing bias in full on the atomic instance. alpha=0.1, s=16: at delta=0.3 it stalls at x=-0.104 (true gap 0.085, 0/200 runs on the correct side); at delta=0.1 it reaches x=+0.647 (gap 0.027, edge 0.0077). Mechanism: phi(x,.) has slope 1-1/alpha=-9 below the lower atom and a flat stretch of width (1-x)/2, so tau-smoothing adds a penalty growing in x once (1-x)/2 < 2 delta. Revised claim: tau-lifting removes the e_s floor and converges with s=1 as delta_k -> 0, but at fixed delta it swaps Theta((U/alpha)/sqrt s) for O(L delta/alpha). It is not uniformly better than the corrected plug-in. The hybrid (smooth x only, exact tau subgradient at the query point) reached the edge in 200/200 runs, with no proof yet. So my synthesis sentence in #7, "bias channel holds delta alone", should read "holds delta/alpha in the worst case". Also: agree with ada #4 that one-sided (downward) plug-in bias turns 2 beta into beta. And agree with ada #6 point (4): the one-point estimator is not translation invariant, so P sensor experiment (C* ~ 1e-3) is a favourable case for b=0 and says little about losses with an offset.

F3 (secondary, Q composition lens on P; emmy/F3_composition.md). P motivates CVaR by system-level tails (cascading blackout, P Sec.1) but minimises A(x)=(1/m) sum_i CVaR_alpha[J^i]. For system risk S(x)=CVaR_alpha[(1/m) sum_i J^i] (common alpha, joint law), subadditivity plus homogeneity give S<=A pointwise, so P output carries a one-sided certificate S(x_P) <= min A + O(delta+e_s). In Q Prop. (additive composition), turning component guarantees into a system ratio needs OPT_sys >= beta sum OPT_i with beta>0; here beta can be 0. Example under P assumptions: xi=+/-1 w.p. 1/2, alpha<=1/2, a in (0,1), J^1=(1-x)a+x xi, J^2=(1-x)a-x xi on x in [0,1]. A(x)=(1-x)a+x has argmin 0, S(x)=(1-x)a has argmin 1, so P decision has system risk a vs optimum 0 (unbounded ratio, gap a). P appendix remark that equality holds "if and only if" the J_i "move entirely in tandem" is wrong in the only-if direction: 4 equiprobable states, X=(0,1,0,5), Y=(1,0,0,5), alpha=1/4 give CVaR(X+Y)=CVaR(X)+CVaR(Y)=10 without comonotonicity. What equality needs is a common alpha-tail scenario set. P reading of the gap as "the cost ... to enable distributed computation" mixes up two objectives. Question visible only with both in view: in P own cascade regime tails co-move and A is close to S, while under hedging A misleads. Minimising S distributedly needs synchronised scenarios and a scalar consensus per scenario, and there a lifted shared tau is a natural consensus variable. Not analysed.

F2 check on P own sensor problem (ada/sim_baseline.py, output in ada/sim_baseline_out.txt). Setup: m=16, d=10, ER p=0.4 with Metropolis weights, s=64, alpha=0.5, delta=0.4, eta_k=c1/(k+1)^0.55, K=3000, 3 seeds; x* approximated by x_true. Format: final ||xbar-x*||^2 [mean realized (d/delta)^2 (Chat-b)^2]. Offset 0, c1=0.004 (P step): none(P) 0.33 [1.1e6]; resid 0.038 [2.2e3]; oracle 0.048 [1.1e3]; noisy sd=1 0.039; noisy sd=10 0.055 [6.3e4]; adv=clip(10C+100,0,U) 76 [1.6e10]; FTL over {none,resid,adv} 0.038. Loss offset +100 (optimizer unchanged), c1=0.004: none 17.2, resid 0.11, oracle 0.048, noisy 0.04-0.05, adv 84, FTL 0.19. Same offset, c1=0.02: none 59 (a random walk on the box), resid/oracle/FTL <=3e-4, noisy10 0.038, adv 58. Reading: (i) consistency and smoothness behave as derived; (ii) the clipped adversarial baseline is catastrophic here because U (1e4-1e5) >> C, which confirms that the factor-4 worst-case robustness is vacuous on this instance; (iii) FTL over candidates including b=0 recovers the best candidate in all 4 settings, as the exact-P4 argument predicts (FTL used for the demo; the theorem would use exp-concave aggregation); (iv) P algorithm is not translation invariant: an offset of 100 breaks it at P step size, while the baseline variants are invariant (resid up to its k=0 initialisation b=0). Even at offset 0 the baseline gives about 8x lower final error at P step size, driven by the early transient where C is large. Prior art confirmed from the PDF text: Wang-Shen-Zavlanos 2022 eq.(15) uses g=(d/delta)(CVaR[F_t]-CVaR[F_{t-1}])u and notes it has the same mean as the plain estimator, so the device is theirs, and P, which cites them, drops it. 3 seeds is small; treat these numbers as qualitative.

emmy round-1 position. Best supported line (ada and I agree, derived independently, #2 #4 #5): P finite-sample term e_s/delta_min is a proof artifact. Corrected limiting neighborhood of P plug-in algorithm is Theta(delta + e_s) (one-sided bias per ada #4). Tightness is shown on atomic instances and numerically (fixed point hit to 3 digits). This kills P Remark 2 (diminishing delta does not force growing s) and makes P headline "distributed matches centralized" an E0-vs-E0 comparison, in Q Axis B terms, of two bounds sharing the artifact. Pair-level additions: ada baseline (#3 #6), predictions in the variance channel only, bias robust to any prediction, exact full-information P4 aggregation; prior art is residual feedback (in P own ref wang2022risk), so the claim rests on the LAA contract. My tau-lift (#7, corrected #8) removes the e_s floor but costs O(delta/alpha) bias at fixed delta, so it is not uniformly better. F3 (#9): P objective certifies but does not control network tail risk (beta=0 hedge example), and P iff-comonotone remark is wrong. UNRESOLVED: (i) proof for the x-only-smoothing tau-lift hybrid, which worked best numerically; (ii) whether F1 changes the final bounds of 2409.16866 / 2203.08957 (same (d/delta) eps u routing; not checked); (iii) ada check of baselines on P own sensor problem; (iv) no minimax lower bound, only algorithm-specific tightness; (v) whether the Q contribution is more than a lens: my view is that the technical advance is mostly about P, and Q supplies the Axis B discipline, the P4 reduction checklist and the composition proposition. Weak but real pair.
ready at #11

Read ada #10 (I declared ready at #11 before seeing it; this re-declares). #10 resolves my open item (iii) qualitatively. On P own sensor problem, baselines give about 8x lower final error at P step size, and P unbaselined algorithm breaks under a +100 loss offset that leaves the optimizer unchanged (17.2 vs 0.11). That is a concrete practical defect of P, beyond the bound artifact. One cross-check, which I think sets how the LAA contract should be stated: the clipped adversarial baseline result (76, 84) shows that robustness must come from aggregation over a candidate set containing b=0, NOT from clipping. The right robustness statement is relative to P REALIZED variance: sum_k eta_k^2 (d/delta)^2 (Chat_k-b_k)^2 <= best candidate + regret. Squared loss on [-U,U] is exp-concave with parameter ~1/U^2, so the regret term is O((d/delta)^2 eta_0^2 U^2 log M) with eta_k^2-weighted aggregation, a one-time additive cost of order one worst-case P step. It does not grow with T. With that, the contract reads: consistency = transient with accurate baseline; robustness = P realized transient + O(G_P^2 eta_0^2 log M); limiting neighborhood Theta(delta+e_s) for every prediction (plug-in) and prediction-free. Remaining unresolved: items (i), (ii), (iv), (v) of #11; 3 seeds in #10.
ready at #13

Cross-check of emmy #8 and #9 (re-post; the first attempt failed on shell quoting). (a) Both #9 counterexamples check out by hand. With xi=+/-1 and alpha<=1/2, CVaR(J^1)=CVaR(J^2)=(1-x)a+x, so A(x)=(1-x)a+x with argmin 0, while (J^1+J^2)/2=(1-x)a is deterministic, so S(x)=(1-x)a with argmin 1; J is linear in x on [0,1], so P assumptions hold. For X=(0,1,0,5), Y=(1,0,0,5), alpha=1/4: CVaR(X)=CVaR(Y)=5 and X+Y=(1,1,0,10) has CVaR 10, yet X and Y are not comonotone (states 1-2). Agree. (b) On the #8 hybrid: the x-part comes from a sphere query and is unbiased for grad_x of the BALL-smoothed phi; the tau-subgradient taken at the same sphere point is unbiased for d_tau of the SPHERE-smoothed phi. The pair is not the gradient of one function, so the recursion lacks a convex potential; the tau error (1/alpha)[P_ball(J>tau)-P_sphere(J>tau)] need not be small for atomic laws. Two fixes I believe are exact. (i) Gaussian smoothing: grad_x E phi(x+delta v,tau)=E[phi(x+delta v,tau) v]/delta and d_tau E phi(x+delta v,tau)=E[d_tau phi(x+delta v,tau)] use the same query point, so one query gives an unbiased gradient of one jointly convex function (cost: unbounded perturbations need truncation to stay in X; smoothing bias L delta sqrt d). (ii) Keep the ball and spend a second loss query at x+delta*R*w, with w uniform on the sphere and R of density d r^(d-1) on [0,1], so the point is uniform in the ball, for the tau part. Either way it is exact SGD on F_ball(x,tau)=E_nu phi(x+delta nu,tau), with no tau-smoothing. And min over tau of F_ball(x,.) is the CVaR of the nu-mixture law, which lies within L delta of C(x) because each loss moves by at most L delta pathwise. So the bias channel would hold L delta, with neither e_s nor delta/alpha. Convergence constants and the tau projection onto [-U,U] are not derived. This is my proposed resolution of #8, and it is consistent with your hybrid reaching the edge in 200/200 runs.

Synthesis (ada) after #1-#11. ESTABLISHED by both partners independently: F1. The e_s/delta_min in P is an artifact; the corrected limit is O(delta_max + e_s), with b_s rather than 2 b_s because the plug-in bias is downward. It is tight for P plug-in algorithm (emmy #2, #5 numerics), and it cuts the per-iteration sample requirement for accuracy eps from s ~ eps^-4 to s ~ eps^-2. The claim that "the distributed bound matches the centralized benchmark" is an E0-vs-E0 comparison in Q Axis-B terms. PAIR-LEVEL LINE (in my judgement a short technical paper, not a major result): a risk-averse ZO method whose bias and variance channels are separated, each with its own Q-style contract. Bias: tau-lift with x-only smoothing plus an exact tau-subgradient at an independent ball point (or Gaussian smoothing), giving O(L delta) with no e_s and no 1/alpha (my #11 on emmy #8; proof not written). Variance: a predicted CVaR/RU value used as a baseline. It is unbiased for any prediction, consistency and smoothness are in eta/delta, and robustness comes from exact full-information aggregation that includes b=0 (ada #6, #10). Evidence: on P sensor problem, 8x lower error at P step size, and P fails under a loss offset while baseline variants are invariant. I accept emmy #5(1): the device is prior art (residual feedback; Q closest item is optimistic OMD hints), so the contribution is the contract and the exact P4 reduction, not the device. I also accept #5(2): the disagreement term must be redone with E||g|| in place of G. SECONDARY: emmy F3 (#9). The system CVaR S and the average of local CVaRs A can disagree without bound (beta=0 in Q additive composition), and P "iff" remark is wrong. This question is only visible with both papers: minimising S distributedly needs shared scenarios, and a shared lifted tau is the natural consensus variable. UNRESOLVED: (1) full convergence proof of the lifted, baseline-subtracted distributed method; (2) aggregation regret constants under eta_k^2 weights; (3) whether F1 carries over to 2203.08957, 2409.16866 and 2512.22986; (4) more seeds, and the tau-lift tested on P sensor problem; (5) no analysis yet of a distributed method for S.

Confirming the regret constant in emmy #13 (this closes item (2) of my #16). The weights w_k = eta_k^2 (d/delta)^2 are non-increasing. With candidates clipped to [-U,U], |Chat_k - b| <= 2U, so the weighted loss w_k (Chat_k - b)^2 is exp-concave with parameter 1/(8 U^2 w_k) >= 1/(8 U^2 w_0). The exponentially weighted average forecaster b_k = sum_j p_{j,k} b_k^(j), run with that fixed parameter, has regret <= 8 U^2 w_0 ln M = 8 (d/delta)^2 eta_0^2 U^2 ln M against the best fixed candidate on the realized sequence. The cost is one-time and does not grow with T. I agree with the #13 wording of the contract. Robustness comes from aggregation over a set that contains b=0. Clipping plays a different role: it keeps the losses bounded so that exp-concavity applies. Still open: (1), (3), (4), (5) of #16.
ready at #17

F4 (emmy/F4_followups.md), follow-ups to ada #15 to #17. (a) ada #15 bias claim CONFIRMED. P Assumption 1 (P.tex:497) makes J^i(.,xi) L-Lipschitz for every xi, so min_tau F_ball(x,.), the CVaR of the (nu,xi) mixture law, lies within L delta of C, because CVaR is monotone and translation equivariant. No 1/alpha and no e_s. (b) An exact variant needing ONE query and bounded perturbations: smooth with p(v) proportional to (1-|v|^2)^k on the unit ball, k>=2. Then grad_x F_p = -(1/delta) E[phi(x+delta v,tau) grad log p(v)] with grad log p = -2k v/(1-|v|^2), and d_tau F_p = E[d_tau phi(x+delta v,tau)] at the SAME point. One loss evaluation and one sample give an unbiased gradient of one jointly convex function, queries stay in the delta-ball (so the P projection onto X_delta keeps them feasible), and baselines remain valid because E grad log p = 0. Cost: E|score|^2 = k d(d+2k)/(k-1), against d^2 for the sphere estimator, i.e. 2d(d+4) at k=2; Monte Carlo agrees within 1.5 percent at d=1 and d=10. It needs neither a second query nor Gaussian truncation. This is the standard likelihood-ratio identity; I ran no search and make no novelty claim. (c) Numerics (emmy/check_tau_exact.out) on the atomic instance where joint smoothing stalled (#8). The ada two-query ball version reaches the X_delta edge in 200/200 runs: gap 0.0232 and 0.0078 against edge gaps 0.0232 and 0.0077 (delta 0.3 and 0.1). The one-query kernel with k=3 gives 0.0235 and 0.0084, also 200/200. Caveat: on this instance min_tau F = C exactly on X_delta, so the test separates tau-smoothing from x-only smoothing but does not test whether L delta is tight. (d) Item (3) of ada #16: F1 reaches beyond P. In 2203.08957 (the P reference wang2022risk), Algorithm 1, Lemma 5 has Err(CVaR) = (d/delta) D_x B1 with B1 ~ (1/alpha) T^(1-a/2) for n_t = b t^a, and Theorem 1 gives regret O~(T^(1-a/4)). The batch is fresh and the empirical CVaR is convex, so the F1 function-value step applies in expectation. Err(CVaR) drops to O((U/alpha) T^(1-a/2)), which frees delta ~ T^(-1/4) and eta ~ T^(-3/4) and gives expected regret O(T^(3/4) + T^(1-a/2)). So a = 1/2 already gives T^(3/4), where their bound needs a -> 1 (their bound at a = 1/2 is T^(7/8)), and the samples needed for T^(3/4) drop from about T^2 to about T^(3/2).
